from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Section details
        lecture_lines = [
            'Finding roots in 1D means crossing the x-axis.',
            'In 2D, we seek points where two functions vanish.',
            'Simple bisection fails because paths are more complex.',
            'Imagine finding a silent "eye of the storm."',
            'We need a robust topological method to find roots.'
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Challenge: From 1D to 2D Root Finding", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Color current lecture line
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        
        # Elements for 1D Root Finding
        axis_1d = Line(LEFT*2, RIGHT*2, color=WHITE)
        # Curve y = x crossing at center
        curve_1d = Line(LEFT*1.5 + DOWN*1.5, RIGHT*1.5 + UP*1.5, color=YELLOW)
        root_dot_1d = Dot(ORIGIN, color="#FFFF00")
        root_label_1d = Text("f(x) = 0", font_size=20, color="#FFFF00").next_to(root_dot_1d, UL, buff=0.1)
        
        scene_1d = VGroup(axis_1d, curve_1d, root_dot_1d, root_label_1d)
        self.place_in_area(scene_1d, "A1", "C6", scale_factor=1.1)
        
        self.play(Create(axis_1d), Create(curve_1d))
        self.play(FadeIn(root_dot_1d), Write(root_label_1d))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF")
        )
        self.play(FadeOut(scene_1d))
        
        # Elements for 2D Root Finding
        axes_2d = VGroup(
            Line(LEFT*2.5, RIGHT*2.5, color=WHITE), # X axis
            Line(DOWN*2, UP*2, color=WHITE)     # Y axis
        )
        # Two intersecting curves representing u(x,y)=0 and v(x,y)=0
        u_curve = Line(LEFT*1.8 + DOWN*1, RIGHT*1.8 + UP*1, color="#0000FF")
        v_curve = Line(LEFT*1.8 + UP*1, RIGHT*1.8 + DOWN*1, color="#FF0000")
        u_label = Text("u(x,y)=0", font_size=18, color="#0000FF").next_to(u_curve.get_end(), RIGHT)
        v_label = Text("v(x,y)=0", font_size=18, color="#FF0000").next_to(v_curve.get_start(), LEFT)
        
        root_dot_2d = Dot(ORIGIN, color=WHITE)
        root_label_2d = Text("f(x,y) = (0,0)", font_size=18).next_to(root_dot_2d, UR, buff=0.1)
        
        scene_2d = VGroup(axes_2d, u_curve, v_curve, u_label, v_label, root_dot_2d, root_label_2d)
        self.place_in_area(scene_2d, "A1", "C6", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        self.play(Create(axes_2d))
        self.play(Create(u_curve), Create(v_curve), Write(u_label), Write(v_label))
        self.play(FadeIn(root_dot_2d), Write(root_label_2d))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF5555")
        )
        # Move 2D scene up to make space for comparison
        self.play(scene_2d.animate.scale(0.6).shift(UP*1.2))
        
        # 1D Bisection Visualization (Left/Right only)
        line_seg = Line(LEFT*1, RIGHT*1, color=WHITE)
        bracket_l = Text("[", font_size=20).move_to(line_seg.get_left())
        bracket_r = Text("]", font_size=20).move_to(line_seg.get_right())
        arrow_l = Arrow(ORIGIN, LEFT*0.7, buff=0, color=YELLOW, stroke_width=2)
        arrow_r = Arrow(ORIGIN, RIGHT*0.7, buff=0, color=YELLOW, stroke_width=2)
        label_1d = Text("1D: 2 options", font_size=14).next_to(line_seg, DOWN)
        bisection_1d = VGroup(line_seg, bracket_l, bracket_r, arrow_l, arrow_r, label_1d)
        self.place_at_grid(bisection_1d, "E2", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # 2D Bisection Ambiguity (Multiple directions)
        box_2d = Square(side_length=1.0, color=WHITE)
        arrows_2d = VGroup(*[Arrow(ORIGIN, v*0.6, buff=0, color=RED, stroke_width=2) 
                           for v in [UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT, UR, DL, UL, DR]])
        label_2d = Text("2D: Which way?", font_size=14).next_to(box_2d, DOWN)
        bisection_2d = VGroup(box_2d, arrows_2d, label_2d)
        self.place_at_grid(bisection_2d, "E5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(bisection_1d), FadeIn(bisection_2d))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#55FF55")
        )
        # Transition to drone example
        self.play(FadeOut(scene_2d), FadeOut(bisection_1d), FadeOut(bisection_2d))
        
        # Eye of the Storm (Vector field mockup)
        storm_center_pos = self.grid["D3"] + RIGHT*0.5
        storm_group = VGroup()
        for x_val in np.linspace(-1.3, 1.3, 5):
            for y_val in np.linspace(-1.3, 1.3, 5):
                if abs(x_val) < 0.1 and abs(y_val) < 0.1: continue
                p_vec = np.array([x_val, y_val, 0])
                # Combined radial sink and rotation
                dir_vec = -p_vec*0.5 + np.array([-p_vec[1], p_vec[0], 0])*0.5
                storm_group.add(Arrow(storm_center_pos + p_vec, storm_center_pos + p_vec + dir_vec*0.3, 
                                     buff=0, stroke_width=2, color=BLUE_B))
        
        eye_dot = Dot(storm_center_pos, color=WHITE)
        eye_label = Text("Silent 'Eye'", font_size=18, color=WHITE).next_to(eye_dot, UP)
        
        self.play(Create(storm_group))
        self.play(FadeIn(eye_dot), Write(eye_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FFBB00")
        )
        
        # Topological approach: Encircle the root
        encircling_loop = Circle(radius=1.2, color=YELLOW).move_to(storm_center_pos)
        winding_note = Text("Topology: Counting Winds", font_size=20, color=YELLOW).next_to(encircling_loop, DOWN)
        
        self.play(Create(encircling_loop))
        self.play(Write(winding_note))
        self.wait(3)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout
        lines = [
            "Domain coloring maps complex outputs to specific colors.",
            "The phase sets the hue; magnitude sets the brightness.",
            "Roots appear as points where all colors converge."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: Visualizing Functions with Domain Coloring", lines)

        def create_domain_map(func, res=80):
            # Domain bounds [-2, 2]
            x = np.linspace(-2, 2, res)
            y = np.linspace(-2, 2, res)
            X, Y = np.meshgrid(x, y)
            Z = X + 1j * Y
            W = func(Z)
            
            angles = np.angle(W)
            hues = (angles + np.pi) / (TAU)
            mags = np.abs(W)
            vals = np.clip(mags, 0, 1) # Darken at root
            
            # Vectorized HSV to RGB (simplified for s=1)
            h6 = hues * 6
            idx = h6.astype(int)
            f = h6 - idx
            p = 0.0 # black at magnitude 0
            q = vals * (1.0 - f)
            t = vals * f
            
            # i%6 cases: 0:(v,t,p), 1:(q,v,p), 2:(p,v,t), 3:(p,q,v), 4:(t,p,v), 5:(v,p,q)
            r = np.choose(idx % 6, [vals, q, p, p, t, vals])
            g = np.choose(idx % 6, [t, vals, vals, q, p, p])
            b = np.choose(idx % 6, [p, p, t, vals, vals, q])
            
            rgb = np.stack([r, g, b], axis=-1)
            rgb = (rgb * 255).astype(np.uint8)
            img = ImageMobject(np.flipud(rgb))
            img.height = 4.5
            return img

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFF00") # Highlight yellow
        
        # Initialize plane
        plane = ComplexPlane(
            x_range=[-2, 2, 1], y_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            background_line_style={"stroke_color": "#FFFFFF", "stroke_opacity": 0.4}
        ).scale(1.12) # Matches height 4.5
        self.place_in_area(plane, 'A1', 'F6')
        
        # f(z) = z identity map
        map_identity = create_domain_map(lambda z: z)
        self.place_in_area(map_identity, 'A1', 'F6')
        
        self.play(Create(plane))
        self.play(FadeIn(map_identity), plane.animate.set_stroke(opacity=0.2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFF00")
        )

        # Color Wheel Legend mapping Angle to Hue
        wheel = VGroup()
        colors = ["#FF0000", "#FFFF00", "#00FF00", "#00FFFF", "#0000FF", "#FF00FF"]
        for i in range(12):
            # Cycle through 6 main hues twice for 12 segments
            color_idx = i // 2
            sector = AnnularSector(
                inner_radius=0.4, outer_radius=0.7,
                angle=TAU/12, start_angle=i*TAU/12,
                color=colors[color_idx % 6]
            )
            wheel.add(sector)
        
        self.place_at_grid(wheel, 'C6', scale_factor=0.8)
        wheel_label = Text("Phase = Hue", font_size=16, color="#FFFFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(wheel_label, 'B6')
        
        self.play(FadeIn(wheel), Write(wheel_label))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFF00")
        )

        # f(z) = z^2 - 1 map
        map_z2 = create_domain_map(lambda z: z**2 - 1)
        self.place_in_area(map_z2, 'A1', 'F6')
        
        formula = Text("f(z) = z^2 - 1", font_size=24, color="#FFFFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(formula, 'A1')
        
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(map_identity, map_z2),
            Write(formula),
            FadeOut(wheel),
            FadeOut(wheel_label)
        )

        # Roots at z = 1 and z = -1
        root1 = Dot(plane.n2p(1 + 0j), color="#FFFFFF", radius=0.08)
        root2 = Dot(plane.n2p(-1 + 0j), color="#FFFFFF", radius=0.08)
        
        self.play(Flash(root1, color="#FFFFFF"), Flash(root2, color="#FFFFFF"))
        self.add(root1, root2)
        self.wait(1)

        # Zoom into one pinwheel (root at z=1)
        # We shift the whole group so z=1 is at the center of the viewing area
        display_center = self.grid['C3'] 
        shift_vector = display_center - root1.get_center()
        
        # Use Group instead of VGroup because ImageMobject is not a VMobject
        visualization_group = Group(plane, map_z2, root1, root2)
        
        self.play(
            visualization_group.animate.shift(shift_vector).scale(2.5, about_point=display_center),
            formula.animate.set_color("#888888"),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # Finalize
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.wait(1)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initial Setup
        title = "The Winding Number: The Mathematical Scout"
        lines = [
            'A loop in input space maps to output space.', 
            'The winding number tracks rotations around the origin.', 
            'A non-zero count guarantees a root exists inside.', 
            "It's like a dog's leash caught on a pole.", 
            'This topological signal guides our search precisely.'
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # --- Colors ---
        DOMAIN_COLOR = YELLOW
        CODOMAIN_COLOR = TEAL # Fixed NameError: CYAN -> TEAL
        VECTOR_COLOR = ORANGE
        ROOT_COLOR = GREEN
        POLE_COLOR = PINK

        # --- Assets Construction ---
        # Domain Plane
        domain_axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-2, 2, 1], y_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            x_length=2.5, y_length=2.5,
            axis_config={"color": GREY_D, "include_tip": False}
        )
        domain_label = Text("Input Space (z)", font_size=18, color=DOMAIN_COLOR)
        domain_group = VGroup(domain_axes, domain_label).arrange(UP, buff=0.2)
        self.place_in_area(domain_group, "B1", "D3")

        # Codomain Plane
        codomain_axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-2, 2, 1], y_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            x_length=2.5, y_length=2.5,
            axis_config={"color": GREY_D, "include_tip": False}
        )
        codomain_label = Text("Output Space (f(z))", font_size=18, color=CODOMAIN_COLOR)
        codomain_group = VGroup(codomain_axes, codomain_label).arrange(UP, buff=0.2)
        self.place_in_area(codomain_group, "B4", "D6")

        # --- Animation for Lecture Line 1 ---
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(DOMAIN_COLOR))
        
        root_pos = np.array([0.5, 0.5, 0])
        root_dot = Dot(domain_axes.c2p(*root_pos), color=ROOT_COLOR, radius=0.06)
        root_text = Text("Root", font_size=14, color=ROOT_COLOR).next_to(root_dot, UR, buff=0.05)
        
        input_loop = Circle(radius=0.8, color=DOMAIN_COLOR).move_to(domain_axes.c2p(*root_pos))
        output_loop = Circle(radius=0.8, color=CODOMAIN_COLOR).move_to(codomain_axes.c2p(0, 0, 0))
        
        self.play(Create(domain_axes), Create(codomain_axes))
        self.play(Create(input_loop), Create(output_loop))
        self.play(FadeIn(root_dot), FadeIn(root_text))
        self.wait(1)

        # --- Animation for Lecture Line 2 ---
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(VECTOR_COLOR)
        )

        t_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        
        def get_z_pos():
            alpha = t_tracker.get_value()
            return input_loop.point_from_proportion(alpha % 1.0)
        
        def get_w_pos():
            alpha = t_tracker.get_value()
            return output_loop.point_from_proportion(alpha % 1.0)

        z_dot = Dot(color=DOMAIN_COLOR).add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(get_z_pos()))
        w_dot = Dot(color=CODOMAIN_COLOR).add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(get_w_pos()))
        
        leash_vector = always_redraw(lambda: Arrow(
            start=codomain_axes.c2p(0, 0, 0),
            end=get_w_pos(),
            buff=0,
            color=VECTOR_COLOR,
            stroke_width=3,
            max_tip_length_to_length_ratio=0.2
        ))

        self.add(z_dot, w_dot, leash_vector)
        self.play(t_tracker.animate.set_value(1), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # --- Animation for Lecture Line 3 ---
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(ROOT_COLOR)
        )
        
        winding_text = Text("Winding Number = 1", font_size=24, color=ROOT_COLOR)
        self.place_at_grid(winding_text, "F5")
        
        self.play(Write(winding_text))
        self.play(Indicate(root_dot), Indicate(winding_text))
        self.wait(1)

        # --- Animation for Lecture Line 4 ---
        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(POLE_COLOR)
        )
        
        pole = Star(n=5, color=POLE_COLOR, fill_opacity=1).scale(0.1).move_to(codomain_axes.c2p(0, 0, 0))
        pole_label = Text("Pole (Origin)", font_size=14, color=POLE_COLOR).next_to(pole, DL, buff=0.05)
        dog_label = Text("Dog", font_size=14, color=CODOMAIN_COLOR).add_updater(lambda l: l.next_to(w_dot, UR, buff=0.05))
        
        self.play(FadeIn(pole), FadeIn(pole_label), FadeIn(dog_label))
        self.play(t_tracker.animate.set_value(2), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # --- Animation for Lecture Line 5 ---
        self.play(
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(BLUE) # Changed from LIGHT_BLUE to standard BLUE
        )
        
        # Change to a Winding Number = 0 case
        new_loop_center = np.array([-1.0, -1.0, 0])
        new_input_loop = Circle(radius=0.5, color=DOMAIN_COLOR).move_to(domain_axes.c2p(*new_loop_center))
        new_output_center = new_loop_center - root_pos
        new_output_loop = Circle(radius=0.5, color=CODOMAIN_COLOR).move_to(codomain_axes.c2p(*new_output_center))
        
        new_winding_text = Text("Winding Number = 0", font_size=24, color=RED)
        self.place_at_grid(new_winding_text, "F5")

        # Disable updaters for smooth transform
        z_dot.clear_updaters()
        w_dot.clear_updaters()
        dog_label.clear_updaters()

        self.play(
            Transform(input_loop, new_input_loop),
            Transform(output_loop, new_output_loop),
            Transform(winding_text, new_winding_text),
            FadeOut(dog_label),
            z_dot.animate.move_to(new_input_loop.point_from_proportion(0)),
            w_dot.animate.move_to(new_output_loop.point_from_proportion(0)),
            run_time=2
        )
        
        # Restart motion for W=0 case
        t_tracker.set_value(0)
        z_dot.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(input_loop.point_from_proportion(t_tracker.get_value() % 1.0)))
        w_dot.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(output_loop.point_from_proportion(t_tracker.get_value() % 1.0)))
        
        self.play(t_tracker.animate.set_value(1), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(2)

        # Cleanup

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initial Setup
        title = "Real-World Application: Stability and Design"
        lines = [
            "Engineers use winding numbers to test system stability.",
            "This ensures bridge designs avoid dangerous resonance frequencies.",
            "These principles also render complex fractals and surfaces."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors for highlights
        color1 = YELLOW_A
        color2 = BLUE_A
        color3 = LIGHT_PINK

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display complex plane with Nyquist plot
        self.lecture[0].set_color(color1)
        
        plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            y_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            x_length=4,
            y_length=4,
            background_line_style={"stroke_opacity": 0.4},
            axis_config={"include_tip": True}
        )
        self.place_in_area(plane, 'B2', 'E5')
        
        # Nyquist plot (a loop)
        # Using a parametric function to create a heart-like or petal-like loop
        nyquist_loop = ParametricFunction(
            lambda t: plane.coords_to_point(
                1.5 * np.cos(t) - 0.5 * np.cos(2*t),
                1.5 * np.sin(t) - 0.5 * np.sin(2*t),
                0
            ),
            t_range=[0, TAU],
            color=color1
        )
        
        # Critical point at (-1, 0)
        crit_point_coord = plane.coords_to_point(-1, 0, 0)
        crit_dot = Dot(crit_point_coord, color=RED)
        crit_label = Text("(-1, 0)", font_size=16, color=RED).next_to(crit_dot, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        plot_label = Text("Nyquist Plot", font_size=18, color=color1)
        self.place_at_grid(plot_label, 'A4')

        self.play(FadeIn(plane), Create(nyquist_loop), FadeIn(crit_dot), FadeIn(crit_label), FadeIn(plot_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Animate winding number around (-1, 0)
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(color2)
        
        # Winding vector from (-1,0) to moving point on loop
        tracer_point = Dot(nyquist_loop.get_start(), radius=0.05, color=color2)
        winding_vector = Line(crit_point_coord, tracer_point.get_center(), color=color2, stroke_width=2)
        
        # Winding number counter
        w_text = Text("Winding Number: ", font_size=20, color=color2)
        w_val = Text("1", font_size=20, color=color2).next_to(w_text, RIGHT)
        w_group = VGroup(w_text, w_val)
        self.place_at_grid(w_group, 'E4')

        self.play(FadeIn(w_group))
        
        # Custom update for vector
        def update_vector(mob):
            mob.put_start_and_end_on(crit_point_coord, tracer_point.get_center())

        winding_vector.add_updater(update_vector)
        self.add(winding_vector)
        
        self.play(MoveAlongPath(tracer_point, nyquist_loop), run_time=4, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)
        
        winding_vector.remove_updater(update_vector)
        self.play(FadeOut(tracer_point), FadeOut(winding_vector), FadeOut(w_group), FadeOut(plane), FadeOut(nyquist_loop), FadeOut(crit_dot), FadeOut(crit_label), FadeOut(plot_label))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Summary graphic: domain coloring and recursive squares
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(color3)

        # Create a grid of colored squares to represent domain coloring
        colors = [RED, ORANGE, YELLOW, GREEN, BLUE, PURPLE]
        domain_grid = VGroup()
        for i in range(4):
            for j in range(4):
                sq = Square(side_length=0.6, fill_opacity=0.8, stroke_width=1)
                sq.set_fill(colors[(i+j) % len(colors)])
                domain_grid.add(sq)
        domain_grid.arrange_in_grid(rows=4, cols=4, buff=0.05)
        self.place_in_area(domain_grid, 'B2', 'E5')

        # Create recursive subdivision in one area
        sub_grid = VGroup()
        for i in range(2):
            for j in range(2):
                sq = Square(side_length=0.25, fill_opacity=1.0, stroke_width=0.5, color=WHITE)
                sq.set_fill(color3)
                sub_grid.add(sq)
        sub_grid.arrange_in_grid(rows=2, cols=2, buff=0.02)
        # Place it over one of the squares in the domain grid
        sub_grid.move_to(domain_grid[5].get_center())

        graphics_label = Text("Recursive Grid Search", font_size=20, color=color3)
        self.place_at_grid(graphics_label, 'A4')

        self.play(FadeIn(domain_grid), FadeIn(graphics_label))
        self.play(domain_grid[5].animate.set_fill(opacity=0.2))
        self.play(Create(sub_grid))
        
        # Add another level of recursion
        tiny_grid = VGroup()
        for i in range(2):
            for j in range(2):
                sq = Square(side_length=0.1, fill_opacity=1.0, stroke_width=0.2, color=WHITE)
                sq.set_fill(YELLOW)
                tiny_grid.add(sq)
        tiny_grid.arrange_in_grid(rows=2, cols=2, buff=0.01)
        tiny_grid.move_to(sub_grid[0].get_center())
        
        self.play(sub_grid[0].animate.set_fill(opacity=0.2))
        self.play(Create(tiny_grid))
        
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Cleanup
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.wait(1)

outline.topic: Finding Roots in 2D: The Geometry of Winding Numbers and Domain Coloring
outline.target_audience: Undergraduate students in Mathematics, Physics, or Computer Science

sections.title: The Challenge: From 1D to 2D Root Finding
sections.content: Introduce the concept of solving equations in 2D. In 1D, we look for where a line crosses the x-axis. In 2D, we solve for f(x,y) = (0,0), which is the intersection of two curves or a 'sink' in a vector field. Explain why simple bisection (left/right) fails in 2D and why we need a topological approach.
sections.example: A drone trying to find a silent 'eye of the storm' where both wind speed and air pressure gradient are exactly zero.

sections.title: Prerequisite: Visualizing Functions with Domain Coloring
sections.content: Introduce Domain Coloring as a way to visualize 2D/complex functions. Map the output value to a color: the angle (phase) of the result determines the 'Hue' (rainbow), and the magnitude determines 'Brightness'. Explain that a root is a point where all colors meet in a radial swirl.
sections.example: Visualizing the function f(z) = z^2 - 1 as a vibrant color map where the two roots appear as dark 'pinwheels' where the full rainbow converges.

sections.title: The Winding Number: The Mathematical Scout
sections.content: Define the Winding Number (Index). If we walk along a closed loop in the input space, we track how many times the function's output 'rotates' around the origin (0,0). If the output wraps around once, there must be at least one root inside the loop. This is a robust topological guarantee.
sections.example: A person walking a dog on a leash around a park. If the dog (the function output) circles a pole (the origin) once, the leash must be caught on the pole (the root inside the park).

sections.title: The Algorithm: Recursive Subdivision
sections.content: Combine the concepts into a numerical algorithm. 1. Start with a large bounding box. 2. Calculate the winding number along the edges. 3. If the winding number is non-zero, divide the box into four quadrants. 4. Recursively check each quadrant. This 'zooms in' on the root with high precision.
sections.example: A 'Quadtree' search pattern where a large square is subdivided into smaller squares only if the winding number 'scout' reports a root is hiding inside.

sections.title: Real-World Application: Stability and Design
sections.content: Show how these algorithms are used beyond pure math. In control theory, they determine if a system is stable (Nyquist Stability Criterion). In computer graphics, they are used for rendering complex fractals and implicit surfaces.
sections.example: An engineer checking the stability of a bridge design: if the 'winding number' of the vibration frequency function is zero in the danger zone, the bridge is safe from resonance.

lecture_lines: 1D roots occur where functions cross the x-axis.
2D roots are intersections of two zero-level curves.
Simple bisection fails because 2D paths are more complex.

lecture_lines: Domain coloring maps complex outputs to specific colors.
The phase sets the hue on a color wheel.
Magnitude sets brightness; darker areas are closer to zero.
Function roots appear as vibrant, rainbow-colored pinwheels.
All colors converge at the exact location of roots.

storyboard.title: The Winding Number: The Mathematical Scout
lecture_lines: We trace a closed loop in the input domain.
The function maps this to a path in output.
A vector tracks how many times we circle zero.
A non-zero count guarantees a root inside the loop.
Zero winding means no roots exist within the boundary.
animations: A scout [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/scout.svg] travels along a closed circular path in the domain plane.
Show the path's image in the codomain; a scout [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/scout.svg] moves relative to the origin (0,0).
A vector from the origin tracks the image point, recording the total angle swept.

storyboard.title: The Algorithm: Recursive Subdivision
lecture_lines: We start searching within a large bounding box.
Calculate the winding number along its boundary edges.
If non-zero, subdivide the box into four quadrants.
Recursively search quadrants containing the topological signal.
This process converges precisely onto the hidden root.

Calculate the winding number along the edges, highlighting the boundary in Yellow (#FFFF00).
Subdivide the square into four smaller quadrants using internal lines.
Highlight a quadrant with a non-zero winding number and split it again.
Repeat the subdivision until the box converges on a domain coloring 'pinwheel' [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/pinwheel.svg].

storyboard.title: Real-World Application: Stability and Design
lecture_lines: Nyquist plots use winding numbers to test system stability.
If the origin is encircled, the system is unstable.
These topological tools solve complex problems across many fields.
